newsitem.title: UK: Xenova shares firm as stock makes UK debut.
newsitem.headline: Xenova shares firm as stock makes UK debut.

text.p: Shares in pharmaceutical company Xenova Group Plc were firm on Thursday as the stock made its debut on the London Stock Exchange.
At 1530 GMT the shares were trading at 216-1/2p, up 1-1/2p from the issue price of 215, in a volume of 307,025 shares.
"We were extremely pleased," said John Savin, biotechnology analyst at Greig Middleton, which managed the launch. "The shares have been trading very well and the price held up nicely."
Under UK conditions, Xenova, which was listed on the U.S. Nasdaq exchange in July 1994, could not float on the London exchange until it had two drugs under trial.
The 22 million raised was 10 percent down on the 25 million stg the company had initially hoped to raise, but Savin said the capital would keep Xenova going for at least two years.
Xenova plans to use the cash to organise clinical trials of its drugs in the U.S., to expand its drug discovery facilities in the UK and to cover expected losses over the next four years.
The group, which develops drugs from chemicals found in fungi, bacteria and plants, is forecast to make a loss of 6.5 million stg this year, having made an 8 million stg loss in 1995.
